When you create a file share, your File Gateway requires access to upload files into your Amazon S3 bucket. It also requires access to perform actions on any access points or VPC endpoints that it uses to connect to the bucket. To grant this access, your File Gateway assumes an IAM role that is associated with an IAM policy granting it. The role requires both an IAM policy and a security token service (STS) trust relationship, and the IAM policy determines which actions the role can perform. Your S3 bucket and any associated access points or VPC endpoints must also have an access policy that allows the IAM role to access them.

You can create the role and access policy yourself, or your File Gateway can create them for you. If your File Gateway creates the policy for you, the policy contains a list of S3 actions. If you don't want your File Gateway to create a policy on your behalf, you can create your own policy and attach it to your file share.

The example trust policy allows the principal service storagegateway.amazonaws.com to perform sts:AssumeRole, which allows your File Gateway to assume an IAM role. Storage Gateway can assume existing service roles that are passed using the iam:PassRole policy action. However, Storage Gateway does not support IAM policies that use the iam:PassedToService context key to limit the action to specific services.

The first example policy statement allows s3:GetAccelerateConfiguration, s3:GetBucketLocation, s3:GetBucketVersioning, s3:ListBucket, s3:ListBucketVersions, and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the S3 bucket named amzn-s3-demo-bucket. The second example policy statement allows s3:AbortMultipartUpload, s3:DeleteObject, s3:DeleteObjectVersion, s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectAcl, s3:GetObjectVersion, s3:ListMultipartUploadParts, s3:PutObject, and s3:PutObjectAcl on all objects in amzn-s3-demo-bucket.

A separate example policy allows your File Gateway to perform the actions required to access a bucket through an access point, with the resource being the access point ARN with a /* suffix. If you need to connect your file share to an S3 bucket through a VPC endpoint, see Endpoint policies for Amazon S3 in the AWS PrivateLink User Guide.

For encrypted buckets, the file share must use the key in the destination S3 bucket account.

# Granting a File Gateway access to your Amazon S3 bucket

## Before you begin

Make sure the following are in place before you create a file share.

- **An IAM role that File Gateway can assume, with an STS trust relationship (trust policy) for the Storage Gateway service.** For the steps, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for_service.html.
- **An IAM identity policy attached to the role**, granting the S3 actions on the bucket and its objects (or on the access point). You don't need to create this yourself if File Gateway creates it automatically. The steps are on this page.
- **An access policy on the S3 bucket**, and on any associated access points or VPC endpoints, that allows the IAM role to access them.
- **A VPC endpoint policy allowing access to S3.** This is required only if you connect through a VPC endpoint. For the steps, see https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html.
- **A KMS key in the destination S3 bucket's account**, for encrypted buckets.

## Overview

When you create a file share, your File Gateway requires access to upload files into your Amazon S3 bucket. It also requires access to perform actions on any access points or VPC endpoints that it uses to connect to the bucket. To grant this access, your File Gateway assumes an IAM role that is associated with an IAM policy that grants this access.

The role requires an IAM policy and a security token service (STS) trust relationship. The IAM policy determines which actions the role can perform. Your S3 bucket and any associated access points or VPC endpoints must have an access policy that allows the IAM role to access them. This holds only when the File Gateway assumes an IAM role associated with an IAM policy that grants the access, and that role has both the IAM policy and the STS trust relationship.

You can create the role and access policy yourself, or your File Gateway can create them for you. If your File Gateway creates the policy for you, the policy contains a list of S3 actions.

## The trust policy

The example trust policy allows the principal service storagegateway.amazonaws.com to perform sts:AssumeRole, which allows your File Gateway to assume an IAM role. A trust policy like this is enough to establish the STS trust relationship the role requires.

Storage Gateway can assume existing service roles that are passed using the iam:PassRole policy action. Storage Gateway does not support IAM policies that use the iam:PassedToService context key to limit the action to specific services.

## Creating your own policy

If you don't want your File Gateway to create a policy on your behalf, you can create your own policy and attach it to your file share. Doing so is enough to put the first example policy statement below into effect.

The first example policy statement allows s3:GetAccelerateConfiguration, s3:GetBucketLocation, s3:GetBucketVersioning, s3:ListBucket, s3:ListBucketVersions, and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the S3 bucket named amzn-s3-demo-bucket.

The second example policy statement allows s3:AbortMultipartUpload, s3:DeleteObject, s3:DeleteObjectVersion, s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectAcl, s3:GetObjectVersion, s3:ListMultipartUploadParts, s3:PutObject, and s3:PutObjectAcl on all objects in amzn-s3-demo-bucket.

## Access points and VPC endpoints

A separate example policy allows your File Gateway to perform the actions required to access a bucket through an access point. The resource in that policy is the access point ARN with a /* suffix.

If you need to connect your file share to an S3 bucket through a VPC endpoint, see Endpoint policies for Amazon S3 in the AWS PrivateLink User Guide.

## Encrypted buckets

For encrypted buckets, the file share must use the key in the destination S3 bucket account.

## Granting your File Gateway access to Amazon S3

When you create a file share, your File Gateway requires access to upload files into your Amazon S3 bucket. It also requires access to perform actions on any access points or VPC endpoints that it uses to connect to the bucket. To grant this access, your File Gateway assumes an IAM role that is associated with an IAM policy that grants this access.

The role requires two things: an IAM policy and a security token service (STS) trust relationship. The IAM policy determines which actions the role can perform. In addition, your S3 bucket and any associated access points or VPC endpoints must have an access policy that allows the IAM role to access them. You can create the role and access policy yourself, or your File Gateway can create them for you.

## Trust policy and service roles

The example trust policy allows the principal service storagegateway.amazonaws.com to perform sts:AssumeRole, which allows your File Gateway to assume an IAM role. Storage Gateway can assume existing service roles that are passed using the iam:PassRole policy action. However, Storage Gateway does not support IAM policies that use the iam:PassedToService context key to limit the action to specific services.

## Access policies

If your File Gateway creates the policy for you, the policy contains a list of S3 actions. If you don't want your File Gateway to create a policy on your behalf, you can create your own policy and attach it to your file share.

The first example policy statement allows s3:GetAccelerateConfiguration, s3:GetBucketLocation, s3:GetBucketVersioning, s3:ListBucket, s3:ListBucketVersions, and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the S3 bucket named amzn-s3-demo-bucket.

The second example policy statement allows s3:AbortMultipartUpload, s3:DeleteObject, s3:DeleteObjectVersion, s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectAcl, s3:GetObjectVersion, s3:ListMultipartUploadParts, s3:PutObject, and s3:PutObjectAcl on all objects in amzn-s3-demo-bucket.

## Access points, VPC endpoints, and encryption

A separate example policy allows your File Gateway to perform the actions required to access a bucket through an access point, with the resource being the access point ARN with a /* suffix.

If you need to connect your file share to an S3 bucket through a VPC endpoint, see Endpoint policies for Amazon S3 in the AWS PrivateLink User Guide.

For encrypted buckets, the file share must use the key in the destination S3 bucket account.

# Granting a File Gateway access to your S3 bucket

## Before you begin

Make sure you have the following in place before you create a file share:

- **An S3 bucket, and any associated access points or VPC endpoints, with an access policy that allows the IAM role to access it.** This policy must be in place for the role to reach the bucket (see below).
- **An IAM role that your File Gateway can assume, with an STS trust relationship.** You don't need to create this yourself if you let the File Gateway create it. To create it yourself, follow the steps at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-service.html.
- **An IAM identity policy attached to the role, granting S3 actions on the bucket or access point.** You don't need to create this yourself if the File Gateway creates it. To create it yourself, see the steps on this page.
- **A VPC endpoint policy allowing S3 access, if you connect through a VPC endpoint.** Follow the steps at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html.
- **A KMS key in the destination S3 bucket's account, for encrypted buckets.**

## How access works

When you create a file share, your File Gateway requires access to upload files into your Amazon S3 bucket. It also requires access to perform actions on any access points or VPC endpoints that it uses to connect to the bucket. To grant this access, your File Gateway assumes an IAM role that is associated with an IAM policy that grants it. Because the File Gateway needs this access, the role and policy are what make it possible.

The role requires two things: an IAM policy and a security token service (STS) trust relationship. The IAM policy determines which actions the role can perform. Your S3 bucket and any associated access points or VPC endpoints must have an access policy that allows the IAM role to access them. This holds only when both the role's IAM policy association and its STS trust relationship are in place.

You can create the role and access policy yourself, or your File Gateway can create them for you. If your File Gateway creates the policy for you, the policy contains a list of S3 actions.

## The trust relationship

The example trust policy allows the principal service `storagegateway.amazonaws.com` to perform `sts:AssumeRole`, which allows your File Gateway to assume an IAM role. Having this trust policy is enough to establish the STS trust relationship the role requires.

Storage Gateway can assume existing service roles that are passed using the `iam:PassRole` policy action. However, Storage Gateway does not support IAM policies that use the `iam:PassedToService` context key to limit the action to specific services. The two cannot both hold, so don't use that context key if you want Storage Gateway to assume a passed role.

## Creating your own policy

If you don't want your File Gateway to create a policy on your behalf, you can create your own policy and attach it to your file share. Doing so leads to the example statements below.

The first example policy statement allows `s3:GetAccelerateConfiguration`, `s3:GetBucketLocation`, `s3:GetBucketVersioning`, `s3:ListBucket`, `s3:ListBucketVersions`, and `s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads` on the S3 bucket named `amzn-s3-demo-bucket`.

The second example policy statement allows `s3:AbortMultipartUpload`, `s3:DeleteObject`, `s3:DeleteObjectVersion`, `s3:GetObject`, `s3:GetObjectAcl`, `s3:GetObjectVersion`, `s3:ListMultipartUploadParts`, `s3:PutObject`, and `s3:PutObjectAcl` on all objects in `amzn-s3-demo-bucket`.

## Access points and VPC endpoints

A separate example policy allows your File Gateway to perform the actions required to access a bucket through an access point, with the resource being the access point ARN with a `/*` suffix.

If you need to connect your file share to an S3 bucket through a VPC endpoint, see Endpoint policies for Amazon S3 in the AWS PrivateLink User Guide.

## Encrypted buckets

For encrypted buckets, the file share must use the key in the destination S3 bucket account.
